raw_response:
*Sitting at the kitchen table, thinking out loud*

Alright, let me think through this year. I've been doing this 25 years now on these 20 mu, so I know my land. Wheat going in this past October already, maize will go in right after wheat comes off in June. Same as always — wheat-maize, wheat-maize, that's how we do it here.

**My wheat (already planted last October):**

I put in the wheat in early October like always, around the 8th. Used the local Jimai variety, same as my neighbors — about 15 kg of seed per mu, a bit thicker than the shop says because the cold can thin it out.

Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about one bag (40 kg) per mu. That's what the shop sells and what everyone uses. Then I'll topdress urea at jointing time around March — probably 15 kg per mu. Last year I did the same and got around 450 kg per mu, which was decent. My neighbor Old Wang puts on more urea but his land is sandier than mine, he needs it.

Water — I've got the well, but the electric is not cheap. I'll water before winter freeze (already done), then at returning green in spring, at jointing, and at grain filling. Four times. If it rains good in May I might skip one. My husband helps with the irrigation when he's not at the construction job.

Spray once for weeds in spring, and if I see aphids at heading I'll spray again. That's about it for wheat.

**My maize (going in mid-June):**

Right after wheat harvest, no time to rest the land. I'll hire the combine for wheat — costs but I can't cut 20 mu by hand anymore, my back. Then straight away I plant maize, no plowing, just direct seed with the rented planter. Window is maybe 5-7 days, can't waste time.

I use Zhengdan hybrid seed, the shop recommends it and my cousin grew it last year, did well. About one bag covers a few mu. Compound fertilizer goes down with the planter, around 35 kg per mu. Then when the maize is at the big bell stage in late July, I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. That's the important one for maize.

Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat usually — if it rains in July and August I might not water at all. If it's dry I'll do one or two waterings. Last year I watered twice.

Spray once for weeds early, and one spray for corn borer at tasseling. The borer can ruin things if you don't watch.

Yield should be around 500 kg per mu if the weather behaves. Last year I got 480.

**Money and labor:**

Family of 4 but my husband does construction off-season and my daughter is in middle school. So really it's mostly me in the field, with help during planting and harvest. I hire the combine and planter — too much for one person and the rates are reasonable.

I can't put in too much fertilizer, costs add up over 20 mu. But I won't skimp either — if the wheat looks yellow at jointing I'll add more urea, better safe than sorry. A bad harvest hurts more than a little extra fertilizer cost.
